top.description: Liverpool hold firm stance on youngster’s future amid interest from European giants Liverpool Transfer News: Rio Ngumoha Going Nowhere Amid Bayern Munich Interest Liverpool have made their position emphatically clear on Rio Ngumoha, with the club unwilling to entertain any prospect of a sale despite reported interest from Bayern Munich and attention from across Europe. According to TeamTalk , Liverpool sources are adamant there is no intention to part with the teenager. The 18-year-old is held in the highest regard internally, with senior figures at Anfield convinced he has the attributes to become a major player for club and country in the years ahead. The message coming out of Merseyside is straightforward. Liverpool “have no intention of selling highly rated teenager Rio Ngumoha” and “any approaches for Ngumoha would be rebuffed by Liverpool”. That stance appears to apply not only to the January window, but well beyond it. Rio Ngumoha Central to Liverpool Plans There is growing conviction inside the club that Ngumoha can develop into a genuine first-team fixture. He is described as “a supreme talent capable of developing into a key player for the Reds and one of the best in Europe”, which offers a striking insight into how strongly Liverpool rate him behind the scenes. That belief has been shaped by what he has already shown. Ngumoha has impressed with his speed, technical quality and willingness to attack defenders directly, traits that have stood out in his senior opportunities. Since debuting as a 16-year-old in January 2025, he has gone on to make 43 first-team appearances and scored three goals. Liverpool’s internal view is that he is “seen as central to Liverpool’s long-term plans” and possesses “the potential to become a regular starter and a top player in both the Premier League and Champions League”. For a player still at the earliest stage of his career, that is a substantial vote of confidence. Photo: IMAGO Bayern Munich Interest Meets Firm Resistance Bayern Munich’s admiration is understood to be genuine, particularly as they assess options on the left flank. Yet Liverpool’s refusal to engage appears to have shut down any realistic chance of progress. Reports of serious interest have circulated for months, but the club’s stance “has remained firm throughout”. Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain are also said to be monitoring developments. Even so, no formal movement is anticipated at this stage, largely because Liverpool’s position is so entrenched and the player himself is settled. Ngumoha is understood to be happy at the club and focused on continuing his rise under Andoni Iraola. That matters. Liverpool want elite young players to see a pathway, and this situation suggests Ngumoha believes his future is best served by staying put. top.title: Thomas Tuchel bemoans Cole Palmer availability by not selecting Cole Palmer when available
top.description: The latest England squad was announced this morning, and once again it only contains one Chelsea player, Morgan Rogers, with Tuchel-favorite Reece James injured and Tuchel-unfavorite Cole Palmer left at home. The Palmer thing is starting to approach extra silly levels now, with the former Chelsea head coach explaining that he didn’t pick the Chelsea starboy due to his previous unavailability. I bet Tuchel wouldn’t hesitate to pick Reecey in the same situation — in fact, we kind of know he wouldn’t — so perhaps he just needs to come out and say that he doesn’t rate Palmer, rather than continuing to insinuate that Palmer isn’t committed enough to the national team, or some other such nonsense. “We have enough number 10s and we stick to the guys who were in the previous camp because we were happy with the two and a half weeks we had together. We have Josh King as a new player in there, but I want to see him on both wings. He is kind of an extra player and he can play all four positions. “I guess everyone is desperate to play for England and Cole is no exception. We are speaking now about a player that is not in camp. It counts when you are in camp and I just said last time that he misses too many opportunities to impress.” -Thomas Tuchel; source: BBC Well, he certainly ain’t gonna impress if you don’t pick him! Might as well be a meme at this point. On the plus side, Palmer now gets to kick his feet up for a couple weeks, play some video games, and be fully rested as we head into the fixture crunch of winter and the holiday period. top.title: Doc Rivers talks Giannis on podcast; 'He's really a difficult guy'
top.description: Former Milwaukee Bucks head coach Doc Rivers, fresh off his induction into the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame and rejoining the NBA media space as a game analyst for NBC Sports in September, took a long look back at his time coaching the Bucks for 2 ½ seasons on a Bill Simmons podcast episode released Nov. 6 . In the 2-hour, 33-minute episode, Rivers went into great detail about coaching former Bucks superstar Giannis Antetokounmpo , whom the team traded to Miami on July 6 after a 13-year run that included a championship and Antetokounmpo earning top-75 status as one of the greatest players in league history. Rivers replaced Adrian Griffin as head coach midseason in 2023-24 and compiled a 97-103 record with the Bucks. Milwaukee did not advance out of the first round of the 2024 and 2025 playoffs and went 32-50 last season. The Bucks and Rivers parted ways afterward with one year left on his contract. After the deal with Miami was agreed upon, the Journal Sentinel published a detailed report about how and why the organization decided to trade Antetokounmpo , and the deteriorating relationship between Rivers and the star player had a significant role. Rivers addressed many of the topics that were previously written about, for the first time in the podcast. Here's a look at some of the topics: Bill Simmons attended the Miami game against the Los Angeles Clippers on Nov. 5 in Los Angeles and commented on weird vibes with the Heat despite a comeback victory. Rivers: “It’s early. It’s early, but, you know? Giannis is; you have to learn how to play with Giannis. It’s unusual that you have a player that’s not like a great shooter but still a great scorer. There’s certain type of things that have to happen. Spacing has to always be right. And you feel like you’re in the way as a player with Giannis if you’re in the wrong space. And he feels like you’re in the way if you don’t have the right spacing. You can see they’re still working on that a lot. “I don’t know if the right prescription, and I felt this in Milwaukee, Giannis with the ball in his hands too much is not as good.” Simmons spoke about Miami trying to move Antetokounmpo to different spots on the floor on offense. Rivers: “I think Giannis, when he doesn’t have the ball, is always hard. You have to figure out where to put him. That’s why I love him as a roller. He doesn’t love rolling. Giannis was the picker and the roller. You look at the first two games in that series he had the ball all the time. He’s struggling with 8.6 PPG while shooting 40.8% overall and 29.7% from deep. Last year, he gave them 15.4 points a night on 41.4% from three. In a vacuum, slumps happen. But on a wing next to two paint-dominant stars, those empty calories hurt fast. His contract ($30.2M this year before his extension kicks in at $16.5M in 2027-28) is a massive, flexible matching salary to move right now without creating long-term cap headaches. This is part of the inevitable evolution of the college landscape, as the NCAA decided to allow for “five-for-five” this past offseason. Five-for-five plays out exactly how you think. College players have five years of service available to them before they’ve exhausted their NCAA eligibility, no matter whether they took a redshirt year or not. What this means is that true seniors, players who got on the field for four years without burning a redshirt, are no longer getting pushed out of the NCAA, but actually have another year of eligibility. top.description: Leeds United Linked With This Liverpool Player: Should They Sign Him? Leeds United have turned themselves into one of the Premier League’s most awkward opponents, a direct, physical side closer to Everton’s scrap-and-set-piece approach than to a passing team. Daniel Farke’s players sit 12th with 11 points from nine matches, built on two wins, five draws and two defeats, the latest coming away at Bournemouth . nigeria.description: The management of the Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN) on Friday said grid instability was not responsible for the Ikeja Electric (IE) Band A outage reported by the company on Nov. 3 and Nov. 4. Ms. Ndidi Mba, the General Manager of the Corporate Communication Unit of TCN, disclosed this in a statement in Lagos. According to her, TCN described the attribution as inaccurate and misleading, saying that the determination of the root cause of disturbances, shortfalls, and interruptions on the national grid was not the responsibility of a Distribution Company (DisCo). “By virtue of Section 67 of the Electricity Act 2023, the determination of the root cause of disturbances, shortfalls, and interruptions on the national grid falls exclusively within the defined functions of the Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO). “IE, like every other market participant, has no authority to make such determinations, and NISO has made no such attribution of the outages in IE’s notice to TCN,” she said. Mba said that NISO had already explained the situation, attributing the current decline in power generation to gas supply constraints to thermal power stations and reduced output from hydroelectric stations due to lower reservoir inflows. She said that the reduced generation had affected the energy allocated to DisCos, resulting in fewer hours of electricity supply and increased load shedding across distribution networks. “The impact on each DisCo varies with available generation and its allocation,” she said. Mba said that the shortfall in electricity supply to IE’s customers was a consequence of reduced generation and the resulting allocation, not any failure of TCN’s transmission network. “TCN can only transmit the energy made available to it and cannot transmit energy that is not generated. “The records for all feeders supplying IE confirm the national picture NISO described. “Of the interruptions recorded on Nov. 1 and 2, 68 percent were frequency-control load shedding arising from low generation. “A further 26 percent were due to IE’s non-compliance with load allocation by the National Control Centre (NCC) of NISO or to faults and works on IKEDC’s own network. “The remaining six percent were TCN planned maintenance, switching, or a line limitation. Speaking to FIFA ahead of the final against Japan in Morocco, Chidi described reaching the last stage of the competition as a significant achievement but said lifting the trophy would make the occasion even more special. “I think it would be a great thing, a joy, and would never be forgotten in life,” she said. “Reaching the final is a very big thing, it’s a great thing and it’s something that we have dreamed of. Their journey to the final followed a difficult start, having lost 2-1 to Poland in their opening Group B match. Buratai, who spoke on Friday in Lagos at the public presentation of a book, Beyond Military Force: A Strategy for Countering Terrorism in Nigeria, said although military operations remained essential in confronting armed groups, sustainable peace could only be achieved through a combination of military and non-military interventions. The former army chief, who served between 2015 and 2021, described the book as an important intellectual contribution to Nigeria’s counter-terrorism efforts, noting that security challenges in the North-East and North-West required a comprehensive strategy beyond the use of weapons. “Military force, however professional, is a shield, not a substitute for governance. The community is often the best source of intelligence, but only when the community trusts the security agencies,” he stated. Buratai disclosed that the Nigerian Army reviewed its rules of engagement during his tenure to ensure compliance with prevailing standards, while introducing human rights desks and other accountability mechanisms. nigeria.title: US reports highest number of measles cases in 35 years
nigeria.description: The United States has recorded more than 5,000 cases of measles this year, the highest number in 35 years, according to an official count released Friday. So far in 2026, 5,182 confirmed cases have been reported across the country of the highly contagious but highly preventable disease, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), the nation’s leading public health agency. That compares with 2,289 cases during all of 2025, and is the highest level recorded by the CDC since 1991. State health officials have reported at least eight measles-related deaths, including among very young children. Measles was declared eradicated from the United States in 2000 thanks to vaccination, but in recent years it has made a strong comeback, fueled by declining vaccination rates and growing public distrust of health authorities. President Donald Trump’s Health Secretary Robert Kennedy Jr. is accused of fanning that distrust. He is known for his vaccine skepticism and has repeatedly disseminated misinformation about the measles vaccine and downplayed the dangers of the disease. Measles causes fever, respiratory symptoms and a rash, and in some cases more serious complications such as pneumonia and brain inflammation, which can lead to severe long-term health problems or even death. Before the vaccine was developed in the early 1960s, measles killed hundreds of children each year in the US. It continues to claim tens of thousands of lives worldwide. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Magazine Books Opens 333-Copy Genesis Book Collector Edition for 3rd Anniversary Bitcoin Magazine Books opened a third-anniversary campaign Friday for Aaron van Wirdum’s The Genesis Book , offering a redesigned Collectors Edition limited to 333 hand-signed, individually numbered hardcovers in an exclusive Genesis Block slipcase. Each Collectors Edition hardcover is hand-signed and hand-numbered by van Wirdum, the former Bitcoin Magazine editor-in-chief whose book traces the people, projects and ideas that preceded Satoshi Nakamoto’s peer-to-peer cash design. The standard package is priced at $221 and pairs the book with a limited trading card carrying a Certificate of Authenticity, a collector pin, a sticker sheet, the slipcase and a digital package. Two one-of-one packages sit outside the ordinary number queue. The #1 package is listed at $5,000 and the #21 package at $2,500; each includes the matching numbered copy, a matching one-of-one collector card and the same accessories as the standard collector package. Standard collector numbers are assigned in purchase order starting at #2 and skipping #21, the campaign FAQ says. Once preorders close, the signed Genesis print run will not be reproduced. The Genesis Book Collector's Edition is live! 333 copies. Individually numbered. Exclusive Genesis Block slipcase. Hand-signed by Aaron van Wirdum. Once they're gone, they're gone. pic.twitter.com/BgiJoCVt8m — Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) November 6, 2026 What ships with the anniversary editions Beside the signed run, Bitcoin Magazine Books is selling a Premium Edition hardcover for $160 with foil stamping, a ribbon marker, stained page edges and custom endsheets. That edition is not limited, signed, numbered or slipcased, and it does not include the collector accessories or digital files. A standalone Digital Package at $9.99 delivers the ebook in EPUB and the audiobook in MP4 immediately after purchase, independent of whether the physical campaign clears its funding bar. Physical collector and premium orders are scheduled to ship in calendar year 2027. Van Wirdum , who discovered bitcoin in 2013 and later led Bitcoin Magazine ‘s editorial desk, frames The Genesis Book as a history of computer scientists, privacy activists and heterodox economists who chased government-independent digital money long before the 2008 white paper — from early cypherpunk culture through experiments such as David Chaum’s ecash, Wei Dai’s b-money, Adam Back’s Hashcash and Hal Finney’s reusable proof of work. Store images for the slipcase and accessories are artistic renderings; the campaign page notes that color, materials and finishes may vary in production. The campaign is operated by BTC Inc., which publishes Bitcoin Magazine . The complaint, lodged with the Economic Crime Suppression Division, also names Mr. Kritsana Kritsananuwat as an alleged supporter who promoted Bitget through Facebook and YouTube channels, the SEC said in statement No. 241/2026. From 2022 through 2025, the regulator found, Bitget offered a trading system in the ordinary course of business, charged fees, ran a Thai-language website that could show values in baht, and solicited Thai users on social channels including “Bitget Thailand” on X, “BGB Thai Holder” on Telegram and “bitgetthailand” on TikTok. That conduct amounts to operating a digital-asset exchange under Section 3 of the Emergency Decree on Digital Asset Businesses B.E. 2561 (2018) without a license, a violation of Section 26 punishable under Section 66, the SEC said. The case now moves to an inquiry official, then prosecutors and the courts. Separately, the SEC submitted Bitget’s website, other domains and its app to the Ministry of Digital Economy and Society under a 2025 royal decree that authorizes access blocks on unlicensed trading platforms. Patrick Steven Yaroch, 37, of Ashburn, Virginia, entered pleas to wire fraud and money laundering in federal court in Alexandria. U.S. District Judge Patricia Tolliver Giles accepted the plea. He faces up to 20 years in prison and is scheduled for sentencing on March 4, 2027. Court papers put the illicit haul at $2,474,380.66. business.title: Rule to Allow Crypto in 401(k)s Arrives at White House for Final Review
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Rule to Allow Crypto in 401(k)s Arrives at White House for Final Review A final DOL rule that would ease alternative assets such as private equity, real estate and cryptocurrency into 401(k) retirement plans arrived at the White House on Thursday for review, Bloomberg Law reported , a procedural step that usually precedes public release. The Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs logged the package on Nov. 5 under the title “Fiduciary Duties In Selecting Designated Investment Alternatives,” RIN 1210-AC38. The filing lists the DOL’s Employee Benefits Security Administration as the authoring office, marks the stage as a final rule, flags it as economically significant and notes that there is no legal deadline for completion. The DOL unveiled the proposal on March 30. In that draft, plan fiduciaries who follow a documented process when adding private assets to a 401(k) menu would get a legal safe harbor under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974. The six factors named in the proposal are performance, fees, liquidity, valuation, performance benchmarks and complexity. Satisfying them does not force plans to offer crypto. It lowers the litigation risk for employers that decide they want to. JUST IN: The White House is now reviewing a new rule which will allow Americans to invest in crypto through their 401(k) retirement plans pic.twitter.com/uXGGIXEzdC — Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) November 6, 2026 What the DOL safe harbor covers President Donald Trump’s Aug. 7, 2025, executive order, “Democratizing Access to Alternative Assets for 401(k) Investors,” directed the Labor secretary to reexamine ERISA guidance and, where appropriate, propose rules with “appropriately calibrated safe harbors.” The order defined alternative assets to include private-market equity and debt, real estate, holdings in actively managed vehicles that invest in digital assets, commodities, infrastructure and lifetime-income strategies. The March proposal implements that order. A DOL fact sheet said prudence under ERISA is process-based and that fiduciaries retain discretion to select any designated investment alternative if they follow the outlined review. Deputy Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling cast the approach as neutral: “The department’s days of picking winners and losers are over.” That stance reverses a prior chill. In May 2025 the DOL rescinded its March 2022 compliance release that told fiduciaries to use “extreme care” before putting cryptocurrency on a 401(k) menu. The department said that phrase was not found in ERISA and restored a context-specific standard. Later, it was reported that Sens. Bernie Sanders and Elizabeth Warren pressed the DOL to abandon the crypto-friendly path. House Republicans have separately pushed to codify Trump’s crypto order in statute. business.title: Binance Hackers Swap About $50 Million of Stolen XRP Mostly Into Bitcoin, Elliptic Says
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Binance Hackers Swap About $50 Million of Stolen XRP Mostly Into Bitcoin, Elliptic Says Hackers tied to the record Binance theft have begun converting a large slice of the stolen XRP into bitcoin, blockchain analytics firm Elliptic said in an update dated through Friday, with about 42 million XRP — roughly $50 million — already swapped, mostly through THORChain. Converted bitcoin from other stolen assets nearly doubled overnight to about 1,650 BTC, worth some $124 million, Elliptic wrote . Most of that jump came from the XRP route. About 192 million XRP, roughly $226 million, remained unswapped in addresses linked to the Binance theft. The XRP was part of the Oct. 29 drain that Binance later put at $6.34 billion. Between 20:05 and 20:09 UTC that day, five hot wallets sent 233.46 million XRP to an attacker address. The FBI has attributed the campaign to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group. Binance has reopened withdrawals in stages and said it has frozen or intercepted about $2.85 billion while covering customer losses from its own funds. How the XRP started moving The stolen XRP sat quiet at first. Early on Nov. 2, between 02:12 and 04:00 UTC, all about 233 million XRP moved into six new addresses, where it stayed until Nov. 5, Elliptic said . From the afternoon of Nov. 5, two of those six addresses began sending XRP on to dozens of new accounts that swapped it, mostly through THORChain into bitcoin. A small amount of ether also went through THORChain into bitcoin that evening. The main bitcoin and ether holdings from the theft — the largest pools — have still not moved, Elliptic said. That pattern matches what the firm saw after the Bybit hack: turn freezable and mid-liquidity tokens into bitcoin first, then attempt cash-out later through OTC brokers. The broader laundering trail is already vast. Since the Binance theft, Elliptic has counted more than 20,000 wallets on 16 blockchains, at least 36 services and at least 65,000 transactions — roughly one new wallet every 30 seconds and one transaction every 10 seconds. About $3.11 billion remains in addresses linked to the Binance theft, mostly as ether and bitcoin. A negligible amount has likely been cashed out so far. Why XRP and bitcoin matter here Issuers can freeze many stablecoins. They cannot freeze XRP the same way, and they cannot freeze bitcoin. After Tether and Circle locked down large stablecoin tranches on Oct. 29, the attacker prioritized assets that sit outside that kill switch. Swapping XRP into bitcoin continues that logic: bitcoin is harder to claw back once it is fragmented across fresh addresses. entertainment.description: With Earth & Sky, her Spring/Summer 2027 collection , Banke Kuku turns to nature’s most essential cycle: the sky gives rain, the rain feeds the earth, and the earth gives back. Reimagining the water cycle as a circle of life, the collection celebrates the abundance that flows from it. Earth & Sky is built around seven prints in three families. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky. The Earth family, Yellow Trumpet and Flower Bud, draws on flowering plants such as Costus spectabilis. The Rain family pairs Raindrop, a glossy, near-photographic print set against the softness of the watercolours, with the Kuku Monogram in fresh colourways. Sky prints are finished with hand-embroidered clouds and raindrops on flowing kaftans and kimono robes. Speaking on the inspiration, Creative Director Banke Kuku shares: “I never start with a sketch. I start with a feeling, and for Earth & Sky, that feeling was abundance. This year I became a mother for the first time, and everywhere I looked, nature was reflecting that same fullness back at me. This is my most personal collection.” A Cycle Of Giving Back In nature, nothing is wasted and everything returns. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back.That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. Banke Kuku also uses digital printing, which consumes less heat and water than conventional printing methods, and continues to reduce its use of man-made fabrics in favour of more conscious material choices. Its commitment to the natural world extends beyond its collections, including its work with the Nigerian Conservation Foundation and its Re-Green Movement, which supports afforestation and the restoration of Nigeria’s natural environment. entertainment.title: Adaugo Nwankpa: What a Career Transition Taught Me About Starting Over
entertainment.description: One year and two months ago, I took a career pivot. I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. In my case, I knew of the opportunity in the energy sector through a friend whom I had met on Instagram. It gets more interesting. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. I went into the interview more confident in what value I could offer and what mattered for such a role. Transferable skills are invaluable Prior to my career pivot, my only exposure to the energy sector aside from buying fuel and gas was a seminar paper I had written in my final year investigating annual shifts in fuel pump prices. However, I audited my skills and qualifications and noted that I also had highly transferable skills. I had communication, business development and a good knowledge and expertise in using Canva. For you, it could be international exposure, multiple languages or something else you think is insignificant. No matter what you are starting over at, you have something that can be transferred from where you were to where you are or where you want to be. Adopt a growth mindset In today’s world, flexibility, adaptability and agility are your currencies for greatness. entertainment.title: Loving Itohan: Come for the Love Story, Stay for Everything Loving Itohan Says About Grief and Family
entertainment.description: Nancy Isime ‘s first film as executive producer, from GREOH Studios, is a beautifully shot story about the love that holds a family together when life falls apart. Some films you watch. Others stay with you. Loving Itohan is the second kind. It opens like the love story you think you already know: a radiant bride, an Edo wedding, coral beads and gold everywhere. You settle in for romance. Then, slowly, the film shows you its heart, and it is so much bigger than a love story. At its centre is Itohan, played by Nancy Isime, a woman whose world is shaken by loss and by truths she never saw coming. What follows is a story about grief, the quiet kind that stays in a home long after the visitors have gone. It is about family, the people who hold us up and sometimes weigh us down. And it is about love that has to keep choosing to stay, even when it hurts. You will see yourself in it. In the person trying to hold everyone together. In the things left unsaid at the dinner table. In the slow, uneven way healing actually happens. A film that looks as good as it feels The cinematography deserves its own round of applause. Every frame feels deliberate, from the rich reds and golds of Edo tradition to the close, quiet moments where a single look says everything. The camera knows when to celebrate and when to simply sit with a character in her pain. This is a film made for the big screen. There is a reason it all feels so assured. Loving Itohan is from GREOH Studios , and Jade studio has never been afraid to go big, with daring, genre-bending stories like Gangs of Lagos. This time, GREOH goes deep instead, trading spectacle for the messy, tender feelings we all carry. True to form, it also hands the director’s chair to a fresh talent, Orobosa Ikponmwen , the latest in a line of new directors the studio has backed, from Kayode Kasum to Loukman Ali. And for Nancy Isime, this is her very first project as an executive producer. You can feel how much of herself she has poured into it, in front of the camera and behind it. Alongside her, Uzor Arukwe, Martha Ehinome Orhiere, Dorathy Bachor, Grace Dein Coker, Chioma Nwosu, Florence Sunday and newcomer Obehi Aburime bring the family to life. Don’t judge it by the trailer If the trailer has you thinking you know where this is going, trust us, you don’t. Go with someone you love. Bring tissues. And maybe call your mum afterwards. entertainment.title: Dayo Akinbode: What Travelling to Cuba Taught Me About Money
entertainment.description: I went to Cuba for the salsa, the cigars, the rum and those gorgeous vintage cars. I never imagined that, somewhere between admiring the colourful streets and enjoying the Caribbean sunshine, I would receive an unexpected lesson in money management. Looking back, I can laugh about my experience. But at the time, discovering how much I might have been overpaying left me wondering how much my ignorance had already cost me. Cuba had a way of making me feel as though I had stepped into a film. Imagine standing in a sun-drenched plaza, a Cuban cigar in your hand, the warm Caribbean breeze brushing against your skin, and music floating through the air. Around you, buildings painted in faded yellows, dusty pinks and weathered blues stand proudly, their grand colonial facades and ornate balconies carrying stories from another century. Then comes the rumble of an engine. You turn to see a cherry-red vintage car gliding past, followed by a bubblegum-pink beauty that seems to have driven straight out of the 1950s. Everywhere you look, vibrant colours, rich history and lively movement bring the streets to life And the cars! Oh, the cars! Later, I would find myself riding in a neon-green convertible along the coast, the wind whipping through my hair as the blue Caribbean Sea stretched beside me. I felt wonderfully alive. Cuba was giving me everything I had hoped for: beauty, music, history and the thrill of discovering somewhere different. I was so captivated by everything that I paid little attention to the money in my purse. I visited Cuba in 2019, when the country had two official currencies: the Cuban convertible peso, known as the CUC, and the Cuban peso, known as the CUP. To an unsuspecting tourist like me, this arrangement was a recipe for confusion. I was carrying CUC notes, commonly used by visitors because that is what the banks give you in exchange for your USD notes. The CUC notes looked different from the CUP notes I would later encounter. CUC notes featured monuments, while CUP notes carried the faces of Cuban national heroes, including José Martí and Camilo Cienfuegos. But at the time, I barely noticed the distinction. Money was money, or so I thought. Whenever I needed to pay for something, I reached into my purse, brought out my CUC notes and settled the bill. I was enjoying my holiday and had no reason to suspect my wallet was quietly making it more expensive than necessary. Then, one time, I was given change in a currency different from the familiar CUC. I looked at the notes in my hand and immediately felt that something was wrong. These were not the notes I was accustomed to using. I did not recognise them, and I was not about to walk away with money I did not understand. So, I rejected the change. Imagine my surprise when the cashier and another customer explained to me that the notes were perfectly valid Cuban money! That was when I got my crash course in Cuban economics. sports.description: Liverpool hold firm stance on youngster’s future amid interest from European giants Liverpool Transfer News: Rio Ngumoha Going Nowhere Amid Bayern Munich Interest Liverpool have made their position emphatically clear on Rio Ngumoha, with the club unwilling to entertain any prospect of a sale despite reported interest from Bayern Munich and attention from across Europe. According to TeamTalk , Liverpool sources are adamant there is no intention to part with the teenager. The 18-year-old is held in the highest regard internally, with senior figures at Anfield convinced he has the attributes to become a major player for club and country in the years ahead. The message coming out of Merseyside is straightforward. Liverpool “have no intention of selling highly rated teenager Rio Ngumoha” and “any approaches for Ngumoha would be rebuffed by Liverpool”. That stance appears to apply not only to the January window, but well beyond it. Rio Ngumoha Central to Liverpool Plans There is growing conviction inside the club that Ngumoha can develop into a genuine first-team fixture. He is described as “a supreme talent capable of developing into a key player for the Reds and one of the best in Europe”, which offers a striking insight into how strongly Liverpool rate him behind the scenes. That belief has been shaped by what he has already shown. Ngumoha has impressed with his speed, technical quality and willingness to attack defenders directly, traits that have stood out in his senior opportunities. Since debuting as a 16-year-old in January 2025, he has gone on to make 43 first-team appearances and scored three goals. Liverpool’s internal view is that he is “seen as central to Liverpool’s long-term plans” and possesses “the potential to become a regular starter and a top player in both the Premier League and Champions League”. For a player still at the earliest stage of his career, that is a substantial vote of confidence. Photo: IMAGO Bayern Munich Interest Meets Firm Resistance Bayern Munich’s admiration is understood to be genuine, particularly as they assess options on the left flank. Yet Liverpool’s refusal to engage appears to have shut down any realistic chance of progress. Reports of serious interest have circulated for months, but the club’s stance “has remained firm throughout”. Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain are also said to be monitoring developments. Even so, no formal movement is anticipated at this stage, largely because Liverpool’s position is so entrenched and the player himself is settled. Ngumoha is understood to be happy at the club and focused on continuing his rise under Andoni Iraola. That matters. Liverpool want elite young players to see a pathway, and this situation suggests Ngumoha believes his future is best served by staying put. sports.description: The latest England squad was announced this morning, and once again it only contains one Chelsea player, Morgan Rogers, with Tuchel-favorite Reece James injured and Tuchel-unfavorite Cole Palmer left at home. The Palmer thing is starting to approach extra silly levels now, with the former Chelsea head coach explaining that he didn’t pick the Chelsea starboy due to his previous unavailability. I bet Tuchel wouldn’t hesitate to pick Reecey in the same situation — in fact, we kind of know he wouldn’t — so perhaps he just needs to come out and say that he doesn’t rate Palmer, rather than continuing to insinuate that Palmer isn’t committed enough to the national team, or some other such nonsense. “We have enough number 10s and we stick to the guys who were in the previous camp because we were happy with the two and a half weeks we had together. We have Josh King as a new player in there, but I want to see him on both wings. He is kind of an extra player and he can play all four positions. “I guess everyone is desperate to play for England and Cole is no exception. We are speaking now about a player that is not in camp. It counts when you are in camp and I just said last time that he misses too many opportunities to impress.” -Thomas Tuchel; source: BBC Well, he certainly ain’t gonna impress if you don’t pick him! Might as well be a meme at this point. On the plus side, Palmer now gets to kick his feet up for a couple weeks, play some video games, and be fully rested as we head into the fixture crunch of winter and the holiday period. sports.description: Former Milwaukee Bucks head coach Doc Rivers, fresh off his induction into the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame and rejoining the NBA media space as a game analyst for NBC Sports in September, took a long look back at his time coaching the Bucks for 2 ½ seasons on a Bill Simmons podcast episode released Nov. 6 . Rivers replaced Adrian Griffin as head coach midseason in 2023-24 and compiled a 97-103 record with the Bucks. Milwaukee did not advance out of the first round of the 2024 and 2025 playoffs and went 32-50 last season. The Bucks and Rivers parted ways afterward with one year left on his contract. After the deal with Miami was agreed upon, the Journal Sentinel published a detailed report about how and why the organization decided to trade Antetokounmpo , and the deteriorating relationship between Rivers and the star player had a significant role. Rivers addressed many of the topics that were previously written about, for the first time in the podcast. Nobody’s panicking in early November, but if you’re looking at why this offense feels so cramped , Wiggins is right in the center of the frame. He’s struggling with 8.6 PPG while shooting 40.8% overall and 29.7% from deep. Last year, he gave them 15.4 points a night on 41.4% from three. In a vacuum, slumps happen. But on a wing next to two paint-dominant stars, those empty calories hurt fast. Pairing Giannis and Bam was always going to test Miami’s spacing. Bam is hitting under 18% of his threes, and as a team, Miami is 21st with 33.1% from deep. The good news for Pat Riley is that Wiggins can be a pretty sweet trade chip. His contract ($30.2M this year before his extension kicks in at $16.5M in 2027-28) is a massive, flexible matching salary to move right now without creating long-term cap headaches. sports.title: Trading Robert Hunt Fixes Cap, Hurts Panthers Depth
sports.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images The Carolina Panthers face a tough choice before the November 10 deadline. They can keep underperforming star Robert Hunt or trade him to fix their money problems. According to Cat Crave , moving Hunt would solve a major financial headache but create a huge hole in the starting lineup. General manager Dan Morgan must decide if saving cash is worth losing a Pro Bowl player who is not playing like one right now. The Money Problem Gets Worse Hunt signed a massive five-year, $100 million deal in 2024 free agency. That contract looked great when he was forming a top guard tandem with Damien Lewis. The 2020 second-round pick counts $24.3 million against the salary cap. If the Panthers cut him, they still owe $10.3 million in dead money after restructured deals. Trading him now saves much more. ESPN beat reporter Mike Kaye noted that a trade involving Hunt would release $19 million in cap space for next year. The offensive line is already a mess. Cat Crave points out that Carolina does not have enough depth to trade Hunt without making things worse. The team is somehow still leading the NFC South, but that lead could vanish fast if the line collapses. Hunt is being paid like a top-tier interior lineman. He is simply not playing like one anymore. A torn bicep last season dented his momentum, and he has not been the same player since. The excuse of playing next to rookie right tackle Monroe Freeling does not really hold up for a man on his contract. What Other Teams Paid Mike Kaye also pointed to recent trades for Cam Jurgens and Quenton Nelson as a reason to consider moving Hunt. Those players both warranted historic hauls in midseason swaps. Should the price be correct, it might be prudent to consider parting ways with the 2024 Pro Bowl lineman. But the Panthers are in a precarious situation. Having invested heavily to reach legitimate contention, their situation is not progressing as planned. You can blame the injuries, but every team gets them. Removing Hunt from the equation would not be the smartest move regardless of how poorly he plays. His slump is alarming, yet the cost of losing him on the field might be higher than the cost of keeping him. Given his disappointing form, it is unlikely any team will offer a deal Morgan cannot refuse. The next game is Sunday, Nov. 8, 1 p.m. ET, when the Denver Broncos visit Bank of America Stadium.

technology.description: ML admins will be happy to learn that one bad GPU may no longer mean starting an entire training job from scratch. The latest 2.15 release of PyTorch includes a rewritten backend for Nvidia's Collective Communications Library (NCCL), designed to improve fault diagnosis and recovery when GPUs work together. This latest feature shows how its creators continue to advance the software from being a tool for researchers to being a cornerstone in production AI work. The interface to the networking library in PyTorch needed a rewrite – it was drowning in technical debt, said PyTorch core developer Tristan Rice , a Meta software engineer specializing in distributed computing, during a live YouTube livestream on Thursday. NCCL is pronounced "Nickel" and stands for the Nvidia Collective Communications Library. It provides PyTorch with a set of inter-GPU communication primitives, allowing GPUs to communicate within a single-node or across multi-node clusters, which is vital for running inference on large neural networks and for other tasks in building and maintaining LLMs. The old NCCL interface was too chaotic The previous PyTorch backend for NCCL, called ProcessGroupNCCL , could spawn dozens of communicators per process group, leading to intermittent deadlocks and unpredictable performance. The new version of the NCCL backend comes with a strict rule: One process group gets only one communicator during initialization. By default, this rule eliminates crosstalk between multiple communicators and all the complexities that entails. If a program requires parallelism, it will have to dispatch more process groups. The updated library also better handles stragglers by allowing for easier reconfiguration. If a GPU crashes or runs slowly, a third-party orchestrator can exclude the laggard and even assign a replacement worker. A “flight recorder” has also been added to give admins a better idea of what went wrong. Previously, if a cluster of GPUs stalled—perhaps from a timeout or deadlock—the user would just get a generic message. The new flight recorder captures all operations in a series of snapshots that can be inspected after a failure occurs. Rice noted the cleaned-up NCCL backend, also called ProcessGroupNCCL, will give developers a blank slate, making it easier to add new features. The legacy ProcessGroupNCCL is part of the 2.15 package as a rollback, but if the new NCCL backend works as expected, the older version will be removed in the 2.16 release, planned for early next year. Like NumPy, PyTorch supports numerical computing, but it also provides tools for building and training neural networks on CPUs and GPUs. The new system, known as Enterprise Information Display System ( E-IDS ), is designed to consolidate data from various systems into a common digital platform, allowing air traffic controllers to access operational information and alerts needed to manage flights. E-IDS is replacing four legacy systems: Information Display System 4, used to track weather and operational info; the Automated Surface Observing System Controller Equipment Information Display System, which also relays weather information; the NAS Information Display System, which relays information about airports and other airspace conditions; and the En Route Information Display System (ERIDS), which handles information about flights. The FAA said E-IDS will improve how Pilot Reports and Notices to Airmen (NOTAMs) are collected and distributed. The agency has had its share of air traffic control SNAFUs, including one in 2023 that temporarily halted domestic flight departures nationwide after someone accidentally deleted a file from the NOTAM system. The FAA said it has already lined up five facilities to receive E-IDS upgrades: airports in Atlantic City, Nashville, and Rochester, New York, along with data processing hubs in Atlanta and Salt Lake City. The agency plans to install the system at 435 sites by the end of 2028. That 2028 deadline echoes the ambitious three-year timetable Duffy laid out last year for overhauling the nation's air traffic control system. Aside from the four systems E-IDS will replace, the FAA has a lot of outdated technology, with the Government Accountability Office saying in 2024 that 51 of the agency’s 138 ATC systems were unsustainable due to lack of parts and funding to sustain or replace them. technology.description: Linux can do many things, but good looks aren't always its strong point. Apple has rather more of a reputation in that department, and a crop of new projects is bringing Mac-style polish to the open source desktop. Some are all-new, such as the Argentinian Lord OS , a whole new GUI desktop on top of Debian. Another, Cutefish , is a revival of a pre-ChatGPT project that never got as far as a complete release. Now it has version 1.0 for both x86-64 and Arm64, plus it's working on Mac binary compatibility via a work-in-progress layer called Reef . Ukrainian Desert OS is already at version 5.5 – practically a venerable elder in this company, despite appearing to be only about a year old. Meanwhile, ClokeOS uses Xfce for its desktop, but underneath, the OS is based on Apple's FOSS XNU kernel. The project lead plans to offer compatibility with multiple types of binaries: Linux apps, plus Mac apps via Darling , and Windows apps via Wine. This isn't new. Much as Cutefish has been revived, last year we reported on PearOS Linux , a very Mac-like skin on KDE Plasma. It has hooks in place for ambitious future features, such as Siri-style speech recognition. What's striking is the number of projects appearing and the pace of their development. Some offer both x86-64 and Arm64 builds, with Raspberry Pi editions in certain cases. For human coders, this would be months of hard work, but if it's just checking an additional box in an LLM development tool, then why wouldn't you? It's almost no extra work, but it widens the potential audience. Coveting Mac-like good looks is a longstanding urge among Linux users, and with legitimate reason. There's nothing wrong with Macs, even if you are mainly a FOSS user. Modern macOS, or OS X as it was called a decade ago, is a Unix underneath its shiny proprietary desktop, and many of the flagship Linux FOSS apps also have Mac versions, from Firefox and Thunderbird, via LibreOffice, to VirtualBox, plus less well-known but very handy apps such as Ferdium and Panwriter. We've written about the usefulness of FOSS apps on macOS before, including for reviving elderly Macs . Just a couple of months ago, we published a two-part guide on how to give Xfce a macOS-like layout and then how to tweak it so apps fit in better . We focused on the functionality, though, not the looks – we don't really care much for such things. If it does matter to you, though, you're not alone, and there are lots of themes and skins to make Xfce look prettier. technology.description: Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) now boasts a system for research into quantum error correction, combining IBM quantum processors with a high-performance compute (HPC) system based on AMD silicon. The Quantum Science Center ( QSC ) at ORNL, funded by the US Department of Energy (DoE), unveiled what it calls a co-design platform for quantum error correction, marrying up quantum and HPC technology. While useful, fault-tolerant quantum systems always seem to be at least a decade away, there have been notable advances over the past several years in the field of quantum error correction, according to ORNL. These include early demonstrations of protecting quantum information from environmental noise, which can cause loss of the fragile quantum states needed for computations. "Solving the challenges of quantum error correction is essential to making quantum computing a practical tool for scientific discovery, which is a priority for Oak Ridge National Laboratory," said QSC director Travis Humble. IBM Fellow and director of IBM Research Jay Gambetta said that it was no longer a question of whether error correction works, but how to accelerate and optimize error correction to build systems that scientists can use to tackle challenging problems. "This new co-design platform for quantum error correction allows us to evaluate different approaches and determine the architectures, software and workflows that will scale," he stated. ORNL's new tool combines an IBM Quantum System Two, equipped with the latest 120-qubit Nighthawk r2 quantum processors , and Umbra, a classical HPC system powered by AMD 5th Gen Epyc CPUs and Instinct MI355X GPU accelerators. According to AMD, the CPUs provide the orchestration and general-purpose performance needed to coordinate everything, while the GPUs accelerate simulation, optimization and the parallel scientific computations surrounding quantum workloads. Also part of the system are AMD Versal SoCs to provide the low-latency control, readout and decoding capabilities for the quantum circuitry. ORNL says that this brings together the computing infrastructure needed for quantum error correction in a single environment, and opens it up to more researchers than ever before. science.title: Record-breaking, fast-spinning magnet could help uncover new physics
science.description: Magnets can be made to levitate by the Meissner effect Science History Images / Alamy A tiny magnet that levitates within a superconductor trap may be the fastest spinning object visible to the naked eye, and one of the fastest spinning objects ever made. In the future, it could be used in experiments searching for mysterious dark matter particles and aid the development of quantum technologies. Superconductors are materials that conduct electricity with perfect efficiency, and they also expel any magnetic field that tries to permeate them – a phenomenon known as the Meissner effect. Because of this, a magnet placed above a superconductor experiences repulsive magnetic forces and starts to levitate. Tao Wang at the Agency for Science Technology and Research in Singapore and his colleagues have now set one such levitating magnet spinning at an unprecedently fast rate. Read more A miniature magnet rivals behemoths in strength for the first time The researchers used a spherical magnet made from neodymium, iron and boron that was about 30 micrometres wide, similar to the width of a fine human hair. They placed it in a cylindrical container made from lead, then enclosed that container in a chamber devoid of air, or a vacuum chamber. Advertisement Next, they used liquid helium to cool the whole setup to approximately -269°C (-452°F), only a few degrees above the coldest possible temperature . Under these extreme circumstances, lead behaved as a superconductor and the lack of air meant that the magnet could levitate within it without bumping into any particles. The team set the magnet spinning with a magnetic coil, ultimately pushing this tiny rotor to 138 million revolutions per minute. Wang says the magnet’s spinning was also very stable: it would take 17 days for its spinning speed to decrease by 50 per cent, something that would typically happen more quickly due to interactions between the magnet and its environment. “In terms of how many turns it makes before slowing down significantly, this is in the same league as the Earth’s spinning,” he says. “This, so far, is the fastest magnetically levitated rotor.” The record for the fastest rotating human-made object is also held by a levitated sphere, but that one was nano-sized, so invisible to the naked eye, and levitated by laser beams. Heatwaves across the world have shocked scientists with their scale and severity in recent years, with heat extremes dramatically outstripping both historical records and the predictions of climate models. science.title: You can see another galaxy with the naked eye — here's how to find it
science.description: null The first time I showed someone the Andromeda galaxy (M31), our conversation did not go quite as planned. I'd carefully worked my way across the sky, starting from the Great Square of Pegasus and hopping from star to star until I was confident I had the right patch. I pointed the telescope, got M31 in its crosshairs and proudly announced to my wife that I had found the closest giant galaxy to the Milky Way . Would she like to see it? She then stayed quiet for a little too long as she looked through the eyepiece. Then came an unexpected question. "Is it near that little smudge?" Hmmm. "Err, no. It is that little smudge," I replied. There was a pause. Of course, I knew exactly what had happened. We'd both seen photographs of M31 — a vast spiral galaxy with a brilliant center, sweeping dust lanes and hundreds of billions of stars. What we were actually looking at was a grayish blur that could easily have been mistaken for a mark on the eyepiece. That apparent disappointment is now my favorite part of finding Andromeda because the unimpressive smudge is real. The light entering your eyes has been traveling across space for about 2.5 million years. No screen, photograph or telescope is necessary. You are intercepting ancient light in your backyard. Technically, the Triangulum Galaxy (M33), about 2.7 million light-years away, can be seen with the naked eye, so it is therefore the most distant object the naked eye can see. But not mine — I've never seen it. M31 is a much more realistic naked-eye target. What's happening and when to look The Andromeda galaxy is at its most dramatic in photographs, not an eyepiece. (Image credit: Created using Canva and a base image from Starry Night) Early November is an excellent time to find M31 from the Northern Hemisphere. It's high and well placed during the evening, and this week the moon is becoming particularly cooperative. science.title: Giant exoplanet emerges from the dark when the James Webb Space Telescope turns out the starlight
science.description: null Sometimes science can seem really counter-intuitive. For example, occasionally in astronomy, you can see more with less light. Case in point: the emergence of a giant planet in observations made by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), when astronomers found a way to block out light from the planet's parent star. The extrasolar planet, or exoplanet , in question is 51 Eridani b (51 ERI b), a gas giant with the same mass as around 11 Jupiters that orbits a star located around 97 light-years away. 51 ERI b was discovered back in 2015 by ground-based telescopes, but the planet was missing from observations of the system made by the JWST. That wasn't a failing of the JWST itself; no one is doubting the observing capabilities of the most powerful telescope humanity has ever hoisted into orbit around Earth. Instead, it was a result of starlight from the star 51 ERI A obscuring this intimidatingly massive world. The brightest planets are 100,000 times fainter than their host stars, meaning spotting them is like observing a firefly hovering around a lighthouse. Even using a tool called a coronagraph to block the star isn't enough to reveal the planet, as that doesn't stop all the starlight. The only solution to this glaring problem is a computer program to wipe out the starlight. "For the past 20 years, astronomers have tackled this problem by observing a different star and using its image as a reference," Jason Wang of Northwestern University explained in a statement . "Then, they subtract that reference image from the original observation to remove the unwanted glare to reveal faint planets that otherwise might be hidden." There is a problem with this process, however. Even the most stable telescopes "wobble." For instance, the JWST requires cryocoolers to keep its NIRCam instrument super cold, and those coolers have little motors that can cause the mirrors to vibrate. This movement, however slight, causes a scatter in starlight. The result is enough glare remaining to obscure a planet, but Wang and colleagues developed a new approach to this problem. Telescopes their more stable digital twins The new approach taken by the team is dubbed Physics-based Learning for Imaging Planets (FLIP), and it involves creating a digital "twin" of a telescope. Essentially a virtual replica that simulates how starlight travels through the telescope's mirrors and reaches its detectors. This twin is then fine-tuned to account for millions of tiny imperfections in the original telescope. The digital twin is then tweaked until it aligns with observations from the actual telescope. Astronomers can then remove the simulated glare from the original image. To assess the validity of the technique, the researchers took a second look at JWST observations of two star systems with known exoplanets, HIP 65426 and 51 Eridani , and one system, TYC 5899, with no known planets. science.title: Hera probe gets 1st good look at asteroid system clobbered by NASA's DART mission | Space photo of the day for Nov. 6, 2026
science.description: null The Didymos binary asteroid system, as seen by Europe's Hera probe. The main asteroid, Didymos, dominates the frame while just a sliver of its "moonlet," Dimorphos, is visible beneath it. ESA released this image on Nov. 5, 2026. (Image credit: ESA) The European Space Agency 's (ESA) Hera spacecraft has gotten its first close-up look at the Didymos binary asteroid system. If that system sounds familiar, it's because it made headlines in September 2022 when NASA's DART (Double Asteroid Redirection Test) spacecraft smashed into it. The aim of the DART mission was to test whether an impact could divert an asteroid away from a collision course with Earth. The purpose of Hera is to follow up on DART by making up-close observations of the Didymos system. "The first thing we said was, 'Wow,'" Hera Principal Investigator Patrick Michel said in a statement about the image, which ESA released on Thursday (Nov. 5). "This is the other side of Didymos from the one that DART’s camera showed us shortly before impact, so this feels like looking at a whole new world." What is it? The Didymos system consists of the eponymous 2,560-foot-wide (780 meters) space rock and its "moonlet" Dimorphos, which is about 530 feet (160 m) in diameter. The DART mission impacted Dimorphos on Sept. 26, 2022, with the aim of causing a change in the orbital period of the moonlet. And it worked: Before the impact, Dimorphos completed one lap around Didymos in around 11 hours and 55 minutes. The DART collision reduced the length of this period by around 33 minutes. The change is a result of the fact that Dimporphos is now traveling at around 2.7 millimeters per second more slowly than it did before the collision. The newly released photo shows Didymos in detail. Just a sliver of Dimorphos is visible, below and slightly to the left of the main asteroid. Why is it incredible? The changes caused by DART were small. But in a real Earth-threatening scenario, even such a tiny shift could help divert an asteroid on a collision course — as long as scientists get enough advance warning of its approach. Hera's observations should help reveal what other changes have occurred on and around Didymos. Scientists are already seeing that, while Didymos has the same central ridge along its equator as before the impact, many changes have occurred. This includes the creation of multiple boulders, craters, and patterns of grooves or ridges. "Since we expect a lot of impact-ejected material to have made it across the approximately 1 kilometer [0.62 miles] of space from Dimorphos to Didymos, it may be that some of these characteristics originate from this transport of material, and we have exciting work ahead of us to sort it out," said Michael Kueppers, ESA’s Hera mission scientist. "We look forward to seeing much more of both bodies and systemically mapping all the changes we identify." Stay tuned to Space.com for more Hera findings from Didymos.

science.description: null The northern lights could put on an impressive display this weekend as a colossal coronal hole on the sun fires a stream of high-speed solar wind toward Earth. If G2 conditions materialize, the northern lights could be visible as far south as New York and Idaho. What is happening? The culprit behind the potential uptick in northern lights is a large coronal hole on the sun , a region where the sun's magnetic field opens up. They allow streams of charged particles known as the solar wind to escape more easily into space. Coronal holes appear darker in ultraviolet images because they are cooler and less dense than their surroundings. And this particularly large — and rather oddly shaped — coronal hole is sending some seriously speedy wind our way. The culprit is a large coronal hole in the sun, shaped a bit like a witch on a broom... (Image credit: NASA SDO) The U.K. Met Office forecasts solar wind speeds between 342 and 404 miles (550-650 kilometers) per second, considerably faster than the typical speed of around 249 miles (400 km) per second. The fast solar winds are expected to arrive around Nov. 6-7 and could persist through much of the weekend. It could interact with Earth's magnetic field , potentially triggering geomagnetic storms and fueling spectacular aurora shows. The stronger the storm, the farther south the northern lights can potentially be seen. A predictive model from NOAA's Space Weather Prediction Center showing speedy solar wind (radial velocity image lower left) arriving at Earth (green dot) around Nov. 6 and persisting through Nov. 9. (Image credit: NOAA's Space Weather Prediction Center) Where will auroras be visible? Under G1 conditions, auroras may be visible from northern Michigan and Maine, but if activity intensifies to G2 levels, skywatchers farther south, including those in New York and Idaho, could be in for a treat. But remember! Aurora forecasts are notoriously tricky. Much depends on the strength and orientation of the magnetic field carried by the incoming solar wind, particularly whether it points southward, allowing more energy to transfer to Earth's magnetic field. science.title: 4-billion-year-old 'Rosetta Stone' found in Sahara Desert could unlock the secret history of water on Mars
science.description: null A rose-colored rock discovered in the Sahara Desert may hold some clues to Mars' ancient geological history. The meteorite , named Teghaza 001 after the salt plain in Mali where it was discovered in 2022, weighs roughly 1.8 pounds (800 grams) and formed more than 4.1 billion years ago. Blasted off Mars by an impact before eventually landing on Earth, it is one of the three oldest Martian meteorites ever found. The extraordinary age and unusual mineral composition of Teghaza 001 offer a rare glimpse into the formation of Mars' early crust and how volcanic materials may have been altered by water, according to a statement from NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California. "It was only after we started looking closely that we realized this meteorite is really unique,” research leader Yang Liu of NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California said in the statement. "One of the paper’s reviewers called it a Rosetta Stone for Mars." A Rosetta Stone for Mars Unlike many Martian meteorites, Teghaza 001 contains a distinctive combination of igneous minerals and textures that preserve evidence of its complex history. Its mineral composition resembles materials observed in Mars' southern highlands by NASA's Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter . Although researchers can’t pinpoint exactly where the meteorite originated on Mars, they have identified 13 potential locations on the planet where it may have formed. "This is really our first piece of Martian crust from a part of Mars we’ve never had a sample of before," team member Lee Saper, NASA’s Ames Research Center in Silicon Valley, said. "It records interactions of water and rock and maybe even an imprint of the Martian atmosphere as it was losing water." The meteorite was initially identified as Martian based on its oxygen isotopes. To determine its age, scientists then examined tiny zircon crystals embedded in the rock. Using a specialized rubidium-strontium dating technique, researchers analyzed individual mineral grains on its surface, preserving it for future analysis. 13 locations on Mars that match the mineralogy and chemistry of Teghaza 001, one of the most ancient Martian meteorites ever found on Earth (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/USGS) The results revealed that Teghaza 001 was altered by water around 4.1 billion years ago, suggesting the rock itself formed even earlier. The mineral and chemical evidence points to a dynamic water cycle on ancient Mars, when liquid water interacted with the planet's crust and potentially left traces of its atmosphere as it gradually lost water. Scientists believe further analysis of Teghaza 001 could reveal more about how water shaped the Martian surface and influenced the planet's evolution. The study also marks the first time researchers have used rubidium-strontium dating to analyze an ancient Martian meteorite , opening the door for the technique to be applied to other samples in the future. "We've only scratched the surface," Liu concluded.

science.title: Taking a Gander at Utah’s Goosenecks
science.description: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory Taking a Gander at Utah’s… Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search October 6, 2026 Tens of millions of years ago, the San Juan River in what is now southern Utah shared some characteristics with today’s Mississippi River. In a bygone geologic era, the San Juan flowed across a relatively flat plain that formed in an ancient marine environment. Unencumbered by rugged terrain, the river was free to take a long, meandering path on its gradual journey downslope. But this part of the San Juan changed when geologic forces pushed the Colorado Plateau upward. Some experts think that within the later stages of this “ still-enigmatic ” history, starting around 20 million years ago, the plateau’s rise elevated the San Juan’s headwaters , which increased the river’s gradient and sped its flow. With that, the water’s erosive power intensified, and the river started carving its winding path deeper and deeper through 300-million-year-old rock. Today, on its westward path to Lake Powell, the San Juan River flows through an impressive series of entrenched meanders, also known as “goosenecks.” An astronaut aboard the International Space Station photographed the stark desert topography on October 6, 2026. In Utah’s Goosenecks State Park , the river runs through a canyon 1,000 feet (300 meters) deep. In places, it nearly loops back on itself, making horseshoe-shaped bends. One section is so curvy that the river travels 5.5 miles (8.9 kilometers) between two points that are only 1.3 miles (2.1 kilometers) apart as the crow—nay, goose—flies. Entrenched meanders in Utah’s Goosenecks State Park are bathed in golden light on August 8, 2016. Photo by Bob Wick (BLM) While the goosenecks are an unusual geologic wonder to behold by day, the area’s dark skies are a spectacle by night. Goosenecks State Park’s remote, high-desert location and 360-degree views of the sky helped earn it an International Dark Sky Park designation in 2021. According to DarkSky International, features such as the Double Cluster in Perseus and the Messier 24 star cloud in the Sagittarius spiral arm of the Milky Way are visible to the unaided eye from the park. In November 2026 , dark skies offer the chance to view several meteor showers, with the Northern Taurids, Southern Taurids, and Leonids reaching their peaks throughout the month. science.title: 'We got it done!' Spacewalking astronauts finish installing next-gen ISS solar arrays
science.description: null Just as NASA is preparing to demonstrate " Max Power " on the ground, two astronauts on a spacewalk have provided the International Space Station (ISS) with the same. Expedition 75 flight engineers Anil Menon of NASA and Joshua Kutryk of the Canadian Space Agency installed and deployed the eighth and final ISS Roll-Out Solar Array (iROSA) on Thursday (Nov. 5), augmenting the space station's legacy solar array wings to produce as much as 30% more electricity. "We got it done!" said Menon at the end of the 6-hour-and-59-minute spacewalk . The EVA (extravehicular activity) began at 8:36 a.m. EST and ended at 3:35 p.m. EST (1336 to 2035 GMT). NASA astronaut Anil Menon (at far right) is seen at the base of the newly-deployed eighth and final International Space Station Roll-Out Solar Array (iROSA) during a spacewalk on Nov. 5, 2026. (Image credit: NASA) Repeating many of the same tasks as they did on an Oct. 29 spacewalk that added the penultimate iROSA, Menon and Kutryk worked this time on the starboard side of the station's backbone truss on the 3B power channel. The two retrieved the 750-pound (340 kilograms) iROSA assembly from a temporary stowage platform, carried it to the worksite by way of the Canadarm2 robotic arm and mounted it to its previously assembled bracket kit. Menon then attached the cables to tie the iROSA into the station's systems but ran into a problem. "We are seeing half of the expected shunt current that we want," radioed Nichole Stilwell, a NASA astronaut serving as the spacewalk officer in Mission Control. "In this current config, we are not necessarily going to deploy." To address the issue, the connectors needed to be inspected. Out of safety concerns — given that the arrays generate electricity whenever lit by the sun — the astronauts needed to wait for the space station to enter the shadow of Earth to see what could be done. In the interim, they spent the time cleaning up their worksite and returning the Canadarm2 to its park site as they would have done after the deployment. Fortunately, they were able to clear the issue. "We are seeing good shunt currents on the ground, so we are go for deploy," said Stilwell. Canadian Space Agency astronaut Joshua Kutryk (at center) works on mounting the eighth and final International Space Station Roll-Out Solar Array (iROSA) during a spacewalk on Nov. 5, 2026. (Image credit: NASA) After releasing two bolts, Kutryk and Menon watched as the array started to unfurl to its full 63-foot (19 meters) length. No motor was needed; the iROSA, as designed, used only the potential energy stored by its rolled-up carbon composite booms to extend itself. The entire process took about 10 minutes. "Today marks the completion of not just one solar array but, over 15 years after its development, eight arrays," said Menon at the close of the spacewalk. "These solar arrays are incredible. science.description: null Hot off the tremendous theatrical success of this year's "Project Hail Mary," adapted from Andy Weir's 2021 novel of the same name, the New York Times bestselling author is rocketing back into deep space with a brand new Audible Original release landing on Nov. 5, 2026, titled " Exoplanet ." Weir (" The Martian ") is executive producing this ambitious full-cast audiobook drama with acclaimed author and ace comic writer Benjamin Percy ("Wolverine") for the first in a series of curated sci-fi projects for Amazon's Audible. The seven-episode sci-fi thriller stars the vocal talents of Anthony Mackie, Ariana DeBose, and John Leguizamo in a wild time-travel space disaster odyssey that also benefits from Lucasfilm’s Skywalker Sound, which provided the show’s immersive acoustic elements. "One crew. One planet. Three timelines. No one survives alone," states the official synopsis. "When a quantum anomaly tears apart the starship Wild Blue Yonder, each surviving crew member crash-lands in a different era on the same deadly exoplanet—hunted, alone, and running out of time." Ahead of the audio drama's launch, we sat down with Weir and Percy to find out more about this exciting science fiction adventure. Andy Weir has already been responsible for one sci-fi hit this year, as his novel "Project Hail Mary" received a stunning movie adaptation starring Ryan Gosling. (Image credit: Getty Images (Dimitrios Kambouris)) When Percy was first approached by Audible about this challenging endeavor, it was part of a bake-off situation where he was competing with several other writers, all jockeying for position. "I think the thing that set me apart is my understanding of how to channel legacy properties," Percy tells Space. "Having written for DC and for Marvel, I can take 'Star Wars' or 'Predator' or Wolverine or Batman and honor that legacy but also put my own unique spin on it. "When it came to the banner of 'Andy Weir Presents,' my job was to write my best version of an awesome Andy Weir story. So I thought about space disasters, big-hearted hopefulness, quippy humor, and a roller coaster plot, and then I nested into all of that a time-travel story." Writing an audio drama is unlike the comic work that Percy is known for, but as he explains, it's also quite different from working on conventional shows and movies too. "If you’re watching TV or film, you’re passive and letting it wash over you. You’re taking in the story as a passenger," notes Percy. "But when you're listening to audio, you're invited in with the dialogue, the narration, the sound cues. You’re invited to fill in the vacancies. As a result of that, you become like a co-author in the experience. I was super excited to jump into this project."
